seo_desc: Marina Christmas events for kids in 2026: a free tree lighting with Santa and Mrs. Claus, plus Santa on a fire engine.
lede: Marina lights its Christmas tree at Vince DiMaggio Park with Santa, carols and s'mores, and Santa tours the neighborhoods on a fire engine the next day.
celebrates: Marina marks the start of the season with a tree lighting at Vince DiMaggio Park on the first Friday in December. The Marina Foundation and the City of Marina host the free family event, and the same living evergreen in the park is decorated with lights and lit each year. Santa and Mrs. Claus make an appearance, a band plays Christmas music so everyone can sing carols, and the foundation gives out cookies, hot cocoa and apple cider. The next morning Santa tours the city on a fire engine for Santa in the Neighborhood. The foundation calls it all a gift to the community.
lastyear: The Marina Foundation says the tree lighting is an annual tradition, with the same tree decorated and lit every year, and that Santa and Mrs. Claus always make an appearance. A City of Marina council agenda from March 2025 lists a project to enhance the holiday light display with the city tree lighting event and marks it complete. The foundation says donations pay for the music, cookies, candy canes and hot drinks, and for new lights for the tree when needed, so the event runs on community support.
facts: Vince DiMaggio Park is at 3200 Del Monte Boulevard in Marina, and it is the home of the city's Christmas tree, a living evergreen. The Marina Foundation says the tree's elevated location makes the lights visible at night for the rest of the season, so families can drive or walk by after the ceremony. The event is held on the first Friday in December every year, and the foundation lists the American Legion Auxiliary and Monterey Peninsula Engineering among its sponsors. Volunteer Scouts serve s'mores at the party.

faq: Where is the Marina Christmas tree lighting held?

It is held at Vince DiMaggio Park, 3200 Del Monte Boulevard, on the first Friday in December. The Marina Foundation hosts it with the City of Marina, and the same living evergreen in the park is decorated every year.
Is the Marina tree lighting free?
Yes. The Marina Foundation describes the tree lighting as a free family event and says everything is free as its gift to the community, from the cookies and hot drinks to the wagon rides.
Who comes to the Marina tree lighting?
Santa and Mrs. Claus appear at the park every year, a band plays Christmas music for carols, and volunteer Scouts provide s'mores. The foundation says all ages are welcome.
How does Santa in the Neighborhood work in Marina?

Santa rides on a fire engine around the City of Marina the morning after the tree lighting. Families listen and watch for the fire engine, and the Marina Foundation posts the route on a flyer on its tree lighting page.
Who pays for the Marina tree lighting?

The Marina Foundation says donations pay for the ceremony, including music, cookies, candy canes and hot drinks, and for new lights for the tree when needed. Sponsors include Monterey Peninsula Engineering, the American Legion Auxiliary and Springhill Suites by Marriott.
